proposed.text: Under PD 1096, when an existing building undergoes a change of use (e.g., from warehouse to mercantile), what document does the Building Official issue to authorize the new use?

options.text: Both a Certificate of Occupancy and a separate Certificate of Use are issued, each covering a different occupancy scenario

A fresh Certificate of Occupancy is issued for the new use - PD 1096 recognizes only the Certificate of Occupancy, and Sec. 309(c) treats an approved change of use as triggering a new Certificate of Occupancy
A Certificate of Occupancy applies only to new construction, while change-of-use authorizations are handled by the local zoning office
An amended Building Permit, signed by the City Mayor, supersedes the original Certificate of Occupancy

rationale.a: Fabricates a separate 'Certificate of Use' that does not exist in PD 1096; the Code issues only the Certificate of Occupancy.
rationale.c: Incorrectly carves out change-of-use as a zoning-only matter; PD 1096 Sec. 309 expressly covers changes of use and occupancy classification.
rationale.d: Misassigns the issuance to the City Mayor and substitutes an amended Building Permit; only the Building Official issues the Certificate of Occupancy under Sec. 308-309.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 recognizes only one post-completion authorization instrument: the Certificate of Occupancy. Section 309(c) of the 2004 Revised IRR (Sec. 309.9) provides that no change may be made in the existing use or occupancy classification of a building or portion thereof until the Building Official has issued a new Certificate of Occupancy for it. The 'Certificate of Use' is not a PD 1096 document; the same Certificate of Occupancy covers both new construction and approved changes of use.
rationale.takeaway: There is no separate 'Certificate of Use' in PD 1096. Change of use = fresh Certificate of Occupancy under Sec. 309(c).

proposed.explanation: Removed the invented 'Certificate of Use' concept. Per PD 1096 Sec. 309(c) / IRR 309.9, a change of use triggers issuance of a new Certificate of Occupancy - the only authorization instrument the Code provides.
